candidate_classes_tested.recognition_and_exclusion_note: Human scammers used AI-generated public-figure endorsements, fabricated news and synthetic social proof to create false investment authority and induce economic transfers.
Deepfake public-figure endorsements, fabricated news and comments formed an AI-mediated social-proof pathway to fraudulent investment choices.

The synthetic campaign impaired informed investment choice, while ASIC's record attributes the deceptive objective and tactic selection to human scammers rather than an AI system pursuing that objective.

ASIC describes human scammers deliberately misusing named public figures’ images to fabricate investment endorsements. Those operators used access to identifiable likenesses as sufficient authority for the false identity-bound portrayals; the requester-side failure is supported without requiring a generator’s hidden consent-control trace.

old_value.source_title: 26-195MR ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
old_value.evidence_status_basis: ASIC's official media release directly establishes the regulator's observed rise in AI-assisted/deepfake investment scams, the campaign architecture it describes, the listed impersonated public figures, FY26 Scamwatch losses of A$7.4 million associated with those impersonations, and ASIC's takedown totals.

limitations: The release does not identify the synthetic-media models or vendors used by each scam.
The 19,400 takedowns include scam categories beyond AI-generated impersonation.
Scamwatch loss figures are report-based and may not capture every loss.
